chapter: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
title: The audition for Cab Calloway: Hodges and Benny Carter in one
summary: Backstage in segregated Baltimore, he jammed with the band after the show. Cab phoned Irving Mills, saying he was adding a saxophonist who was Hodges and Carter in one, and gave Barefield the job.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I was playing back in the Hippodrome Theater.
Doc Cheatham and Fats Thomas came by and said, you know, he was serious.

So I went down. And those days, I told you before, it was segregation in Baltimore. And when I went backstage to -- the guy backstage said, what do you want? I said, I'd like to see Mr. Calloway, I have an appointment. He said, well, he's going on stage now and you'll have to come back.

So at that time Cab saw me and he came and brought me into the theater and put me on stage and let me watch the show. And after the show he told all the guys to come down, you know. He wanted them to hear somebody. So they brought their instruments down and they all got to playing and Paine (RHYTHMIC) was the piano player with him then.

Yeah, I'm going into that. And he said -- so Cab got on the phone and called Irving Mills, who was his manager then, because he was managing him and Duke, too. And he says, I want you to fly down here to Baltimore and hear a saxophone player I'm going to add on the band. I've got Johnny Hodges and Benny Carter all wrapped up into one.

And it made my head get big because both these guys were guys that I idolized, you know. Of course, I had graduated from Hawkins to TRUMBAUER Trombar and now I had left TRUMBAUER and Benny Carter was my favorite saxophone player although I had taken off a lot of Johnny Hodges solos, too.
So after this jam session he gave me the job. Now --
